memory_candidates.content: verify-deploy.sh's gate 5 (manifest-driven parity + content-hash equality, via lua/neotex/plugins/ai/shared/extensions/verify.lua) is one-directional: it only checks that declared/manifest-listed files are present and hash-match in the deployed tree. It has no 'extra'/'orphan' field and never scans the deployed tree for undeclared content. Orphaned files with no source-store owner (e.g. left behind after a source file is deleted/renamed, since install-extension.sh's merge_index_entries() is purely additive with no stale-removal step) will pass this gate forever. Any future 'declared vs deployed parity' claim must be read as this one-directional guarantee, not a bidirectional one, unless a subtractive/orphan-detection pass is added.

Technique for testing deploy-headless.sh idempotency/byte-identity safely: global_extensions_dir in lua/neotex/plugins/ai/shared/extensions/config.lua is hardcoded to ~/.config/nvim/agent-system/extensions regardless of the TARGET_REPO argument, so deploy-headless.sh --wipe <scratch-git-repo> can be run against an arbitrary scratch git repo (seeded with a copy of the live .claude-extensions.json to replicate the same active-extension set) without touching the live .claude/ tree. Running it twice on the same scratch target and diffing the two .claude/ trees is the correct way to test byte-identical-twice claims.

run-all.sh (the shell test suite runner) behaves differently when run from its source-store location (agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/tests/run-all.sh) versus its deployed location (.claude/scripts/tests/run-all.sh): a REPO_ROOT path-depth resolution bug in the deployed copy causes 5 additional suite failures (missing-file errors resolving to /home/benjamin/... instead of /home/benjamin/.config/nvim/...) that do not occur in source-store mode, plus at least one suite (test-common-lib.sh) that only fails in deployed mode for a different reason (a single-source-of-truth assertion catching .opencode/scripts/command-gate-in.sh's un-migrated inline session-ID generator). Always run and report both copies separately when diagnosing run-all.sh failures -- the failure sets are not the same.
